name: Microservices with a message broker
summary: Five services, each deployed and scaled on its own with its own database: an API gateway, tasks, escalation, triage and notification. Services publish events to a message broker that the team runs itself.

components.name: Browsers, API clients and the support inbox
API gateway: authentication and rate limits
Self-hosted message broker, run by the team

flows.data: ticket text out; suggested labels back

boundaries.TB5: Gateway and services on the internal network

ESC-N01: triage-svc publishes suggestions as events; every consumer must ignore unconfirmed ones, a rule kept by contract between services rather than in one place.
ESC-N03: Each service checks permissions itself or calls a shared one; audit entries are spread across four databases, each needing 400-day retention.
ESC-N04: A cap across all rules needs one count shared by escalation-svc and notify-svc; a distributed counter or a second source of truth.
ESC-N05: Target validation lives in escalation-svc; either option can do it.
ESC-N06: The rule change and its notification cross the broker; the outbox pattern makes it reliable at extra cost.
ESC-N07: Task content crosses the internal network and the broker; every consumer and the broker's retention must keep titles out of outbound messages.
ESC-N09: Each service fails on its own, but a step needs seven components up to fire; more dashboards to watch.
ESC-N10: A self-hosted broker is not a paid messaging service, but it joins the services escalation calls, so ESC-AC31's list of only email and webhooks would need amending.
CON-1: Five pipelines, four databases and a broker for one rota of eight; each service needs an owner on call.
CON-2: Five deploys a day on one train; a cross-service change needs versioned contracts and an ordered rollout.
CON-3: The gateway is the natural single place for the limit.
CON-4: The gateway hands tickets to triage-svc asynchronously; no request waits for the model.
CON-5: notify-svc owns deliveries and retries; the same idempotency rule applies.
CON-6: triage-svc scales on its own, without scaling the other four services.
